Agreed - the support list is diagnostic truth but prescriptive poison for an automated caller: it dangles the cheapest escape (switch harness) before the reason the harness was chosen (model, cost, session semantics). Recorded as [D8](lucid:d8-decision): the hint concept exists, as refusal-attached data. Message order becomes: statement, nearest-alternative hint for the CURRENT harness, support list last. Concretely: 'tools is not available on codex. Nearest control on codex: category switches (--enable/--disable <FEATURE>) or sandbox modes. Supported on: claude (--allowedTools).' And the refusal event carries hint and supportedBy as separate structured fields, so a programmatic caller decides from data instead of prose-scanning. One cost to note: nearest-alternative hints are curatorial - a human judgment per dimension per harness, stamped and versioned like the rest - they cannot be derived mechanically from the descriptors.

On muse's two skills flags, from live help: muse scopes skills by trust, not a simple on/off. --no-foreign-personal-context excludes rules and skills that come from your personal context (other machines/workspaces) for that run. --trust-workspace opts IN to loading the current workspace's own skills and rules - it does not save trust, and muse's help groups it under Safety: approval and sandbox are ON by default, workspace trust is not. what do you mean, "into provenance"

Provenance is the per-run record of where every resolved setting came from - the mechanism from the defaults design (gap 11 there). For each dimension it records: the final value, and the tier that supplied it (built-in profile, user config, project config, or arg). For tool grants it adds one more fact: which names matched curated descriptor entries and which were unmapped pass-throughs. Example line in hcn inspect: 'tools: bash, read (curated) + my-ext-tool (unmapped)'. Why it carries the extensible rule: hcn cannot tell a real extension tool from a typo - both are unknown names. Refusing would break every extension user; passing silently would hide every typo (claude ignores unknown names without error). Passing plus recording means the run always shows exactly what was emitted and which grants hcn could not vouch for. Definition added inline at [D3](lucid:d3-normalized).
